newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech mkt heavyweights hit year-highs at PSE fix.
newsitem.headline: Czech mkt heavyweights hit year-highs at PSE fix.

text.p: Shares of SPT Telecom and CEZ, the Prague Stock Exchange's two most-capitalised issues, hit year highs at the bourse's daily price fixing on Thursday, but dealers said the prices are being boosted on thin volumes.
SPT Telecom shares, which account for 20 percent of the PSE's market capitalisation, jumped 85 crowns to 3,660, while CEZ, which account for 14 percent, rose 34 crowns to 1,193.

"Volumes are very thin, when you come to the market looking for a bigger parcel of shares it doesn't take much interest to move the prices. But the truth is, not a lot of foreign money is flowing in," said Jan Sykora of Wood and Company.
Dealers said they did not see any fundamental reasons for SPT shares to rise much further, but that CEZ could climb another two or three percent.

"CEZ lagged behind other major issues on the market last year, and I think it is now catching up. It could go a little higher, maybe as much as three percent, but I expect it will then level off," said one foreign broker.
Gains by the two helped push the PSE's PX50 index to a year-high as well. The index was up 6.4 points, or 1.1 percent, at the fixing to 586.5.
